### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7605e0c9cca2b890e48a47117d4518ae9c602f27` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

2. **Premise measured** — both PATCH shapes (Entra path-addressed, Okta path-less) re-measured through `AuthManager.handleRequest` with a real SCIM bearer on current main: `displayName`, `name.formatted`, `sys_user.name` stay on the old name. Registration ablation: patch row removed + reinstall ⇒ `Tests 6 failed | 2 passed (8)` (the two passing are the explicit-name CONTROLs); restored ⇒ `8 passed (8)`.
3. **Gates at this head** — 60 success · 12 expected skip · 0 failed · 0 pending; Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check `success`. NOT governed (+429/−2).
4. **Read by the seat** — the patch: 4 lines in the vendor's `setNamePart`, recomposing through the vendor's own `composeName` / `setFormattedName` only when `name.formatted` equalled the composed parts before the change — the ruling's "the same test `setFormattedName` already makes". Header names the ruling and the removal condition, as the ruling requires; registered in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` beside the three existing patches (no other better-auth patch). The vendor package ships only `dist/index.mjs` (`exports['.'].default`), so the one patched file covers every runtime import. `skip-changeset` holds: the published `@objectstack/plugin-auth` tarball is byte-unchanged (patched line in 0 files of its `dist/`, positive control: it imports `@better-auth/scim`); a pnpm patch reaches installs of this workspace only.
5. **Dev's open question** — the value test also recomposes an IdP-supplied name that equals the composed parts, which the vendor's own suite pins as preserved. Answered **A, per the ruling's own words** (the value test is the ruled test); the upstream draft changes that vendor fixture, and a vendor refusal of it comes back as a new decision then (item (3) would not fire). Recorded here, no ruling owed now.
6. **Out of scope** — an npm install of the published `plugin-auth` resolves an unpatched vendor until the vendor ships (the ruling's item (3), `Acceptance notes`); the ruling's note that cloud's SCIM known-issue line can go once this lands → cloud's lane (the seat tells cloud at merge); an email-seeded `name.formatted` is not recomposed (`Acceptance notes`). L2: not owed (no contract face).

**Landing** — non-governed, ≤3000 lines: the seat lands it through the ordinary queue.
